\chapter{Learning Theory — Finite Minimax}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.LearningTheory.Minimax.FiniteMinimax
\section{Overview}

This module develops finite two-player zero-sum games and proves an approximate
minimax theorem via the Hedge (multiplicative weights) algorithm.  The main
results are weak duality---showing that the row player's mixed-strategy minimum
payoff never exceeds the column player's mixed-strategy maximum payoff---and
\texttt{approx\_minimax}, which constructs an $\varepsilon$-approximate saddle
point for any $\varepsilon > 0$ by running Hedge for sufficiently many rounds
against column best responses.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Finite zero-sum game]
\lean{ZeroSumGame}
\label{ZeroSumGame}
\leanok
A \emph{finite two-player zero-sum game} with $M$ row actions and $N$ column
actions is a record consisting of a payoff matrix $A : \mathrm{Fin}\,M \to
\mathrm{Fin}\,N \to \mathbb{R}$ together with proofs that every entry satisfies
$0 \le A_{ij} \le 1$.  The row player seeks to maximise the payoff; the column
player seeks to minimise it.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Mixed strategy]
\lean{MixedStrategy}
\label{MixedStrategy}
\leanok
A \emph{mixed strategy} over $n$ actions is a record consisting of a weight
function $w : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathbb{R}$ together with proofs that every
weight is non-negative and that the weights sum to $1$, i.e.\ $w$ is a
probability distribution over $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Row mixed payoff against a pure column]
\lean{payoffVsPure}
\label{payoffVsPure}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, ZeroSumGame}
Given a game $G$, a mixed row strategy $p$, and a pure column $j$, the
\emph{expected payoff against column $j$} is
\[
  \mathrm{payoffVsPure}(G, p, j) \;=\; \sum_{i} p_i \cdot A_{ij}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Pure row payoff against a mixed column]
\lean{pureVsPayoff}
\label{pureVsPayoff}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, ZeroSumGame}
Given a game $G$, a pure row $i$, and a mixed column strategy $q$, the
\emph{expected payoff of row $i$ against $q$} is
\[
  \mathrm{pureVsPayoff}(G, i, q) \;=\; \sum_{j} A_{ij} \cdot q_j.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Column best response]
\lean{bestColumn}
\label{bestColumn}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, ZeroSumGame, payoffVsPure}
Given a game $G$ and a mixed row strategy $p$, \texttt{bestColumn} is the pure
column $j^* \in \mathrm{Fin}\,N$ that minimises $\mathrm{payoffVsPure}(G, p,
\cdot)$, chosen via the classical axiom of choice from the finite minimiser.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Optimality of the column best response]
\lean{bestColumn_spec}
\label{bestColumn_spec}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, ZeroSumGame, bestColumn, payoffVsPure}
\difficulty{1}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M$ row actions and $N \ge 1$ column
actions, given by a payoff matrix $A_{ij} \in [0,1]$, and let $p$ be a mixed strategy
for the row player, with weights $p_i$. Write $v(j) = \sum_i p_i A_{ij}$ for the
expected payoff of $p$ against the pure column $j$, and let $j^*$ be a column that
minimises $v$ over all $N$ columns. Then $v(j^*) \le v(j)$ for every column $j$; that
is, $j^*$ is indeed a minimiser of the expected payoff against $p$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Row best response]
\lean{bestRow}
\label{bestRow}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, ZeroSumGame, pureVsPayoff}
Given a game $G$ and a mixed column strategy $q$, \texttt{bestRow} is the pure
row $i^* \in \mathrm{Fin}\,M$ that maximises $\mathrm{pureVsPayoff}(G, \cdot,
q)$, chosen classically from the finite maximiser.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Optimality of the row best response]
\lean{bestRow_spec}
\label{bestRow_spec}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, ZeroSumGame, bestRow, pureVsPayoff}
\difficulty{1}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with a nonempty set of $M$ row actions and
$N$ column actions, given by a payoff matrix $A$ with $0 \le A_{ij} \le 1$, and let $q$
be a mixed strategy for the column player. For a pure row $i$, write $u(i) = \sum_{j}
A_{ij}\, q_j$ for its expected payoff against $q$, and let $i^\ast$ be a row maximising
$u$. Then $u(i) \le u(i^\ast)$ for every row $i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Weak duality for finite zero-sum games]
\lean{weak_duality}
\label{weak_duality}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, ZeroSumGame, ZeroSumGame.toLossSeq, payoffVsPure, pureVsPayoff}
\difficulty{5}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M \ge 1$ row actions and $N \ge 1$
column actions, given by a payoff matrix $A$ whose entries satisfy $A_{ij} \in [0,1]$,
where the row player maximises and the column player minimises. Let $p = (p_i)$ be a
mixed strategy for the row player and $q = (q_j)$ a mixed strategy for the column
player. Then the row player's guaranteed payoff under $p$ never exceeds the payoff the
column player can be forced above under $q$:
\[
  \min_{j} \sum_{i} p_i\, A_{ij} \;\le\; \max_{i} \sum_{j} A_{ij}\, q_j .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Loss sequence induced by a game]
\lean{ZeroSumGame.toLossSeq}
\label{ZeroSumGame.toLossSeq}
\leanok
\uses{LossSeq, ZeroSumGame}
Given a game $G$ and a sequence of column responses $j_0, \dots, j_{T-1}$, the
induced \emph{loss sequence} for the row player is $\ell_t(i) = 1 - A_{i,j_t}
\in [0,1]$.  This translates a zero-sum game into the abstract loss-sequence
framework used by Hedge.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Validity of the loss sequence induced by a zero-sum game]
\lean{ZeroSumGame.toLossSeq_valid}
\label{ZeroSumGame.toLossSeq_valid}
\leanok
\uses{LossSeq.Valid, ZeroSumGame, ZeroSumGame.toLossSeq}
\difficulty{2}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M$ row actions and $N$ column
actions, given by a payoff matrix $A$ whose entries satisfy $0 \le A_{ij} \le 1$, and
let $j_0, \dots, j_{T-1}$ be any sequence of column responses. Then the induced loss
sequence for the row player, defined by $\ell_t(i) = 1 - A_{i,j_t}$ for each round $t <
T$ and row action $i$, is valid: every loss lies in $[0,1]$, i.e. $0 \le \ell_t(i) \le
1$ for all $t$ and $i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Average strategy]
\lean{averageStrategy}
\label{averageStrategy}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy}
Given $T$ distributions $p_0, \dots, p_{T-1}$ over $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ (each
presented as non-negative weights summing to $1$) and $T > 0$, the
\emph{average strategy} is the mixed strategy with weights
\[
  \bar{p}_i \;=\; \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} p_t(i).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Hedge mixed strategy]
\lean{hedgeMixedStrategy}
\label{hedgeMixedStrategy}
\leanok
\uses{LossSeq, MixedStrategy, hedgeDist, hedgeDist_nonneg, hedgeDist_sum}
The Hedge distribution at round $t$ for learning rate $\eta$ and loss sequence
$\ell$, packaged as a \texttt{MixedStrategy} by bundling the non-negativity and
sum-one proofs from \texttt{hedgeDist}.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Empirical strategy]
\lean{empiricalStrategy}
\label{empiricalStrategy}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy}
Given $T > 0$ pure actions $a_0, \dots, a_{T-1} \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, the
\emph{empirical strategy} is the mixed strategy assigning to each $i$ the
fraction of rounds on which action $i$ was played:
\[
  q_i \;=\; \frac{1}{T}\#\{t : a_t = i\}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Average strategy's payoff against a pure column]
\lean{payoffVsPure_averageStrategy}
\label{payoffVsPure_averageStrategy}
\leanok
\uses{ZeroSumGame, averageStrategy, payoffVsPure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M \ge 1$ row actions and $N$ column
actions, given by a payoff matrix $A$ with $0 \le A_{ij} \le 1$, and fix a pure column
action $j$. Let $T > 0$ and let $p_0, \dots, p_{T-1}$ be probability distributions over
the $M$ row actions, each presented as non-negative weights $p_t(i)$ summing to $1$, and
let $\bar{p}$ be their average strategy, the mixed row strategy with weights $\bar{p}_i
= \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1} p_t(i)$. Then the expected payoff of $\bar{p}$ against
column $j$ satisfies
\[
  \sum_{i} \bar{p}_i \, A_{ij}
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \sum_{i} p_t(i) \, A_{ij}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Pure-row payoff against the empirical column strategy]
\lean{pureVsPayoff_empiricalStrategy}
\label{pureVsPayoff_empiricalStrategy}
\leanok
\uses{ZeroSumGame, empiricalStrategy, pureVsPayoff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M$ row actions and $N \ge 1$ column
actions, and payoff matrix $A$. Fix a row action $i$ and a sequence of column actions
$a_0, \dots, a_{T-1}$ with $T > 0$, and let $\hat{q}$ be the associated empirical column
strategy. Then the expected payoff of row $i$ against $\hat{q}$ equals the average
payoff over the sequence:
\[
  \sum_{j} A_{ij}\,\hat{q}_j \;=\; \frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1} A_{i,\,a_t}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Prefix cumulative game loss]
\lean{prefixGameLoss}
\label{prefixGameLoss}
\leanok
\uses{ZeroSumGame}
Given a game $G$, a prefix of $t$ column actions, and a row $i$, the
\emph{prefix cumulative loss} of row $i$ is
\[
  L_t(i) \;=\; \sum_{s=0}^{t-1} \bigl(1 - A_{i, a_s}\bigr).
\]
This mirrors \texttt{cumLoss} from the abstract Hedge framework, expressed
directly in terms of game payoffs.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Prefix Hedge weight]
\lean{prefixHedgeWeight}
\label{prefixHedgeWeight}
\leanok
\uses{ZeroSumGame, prefixGameLoss}
The unnormalised Hedge weight of row $i$ after seeing a prefix of column
actions at learning rate $\eta$ is
\[
  w_t(i) \;=\; \exp\!\bigl(-\eta \cdot L_t(i)\bigr),
\]
where $L_t(i)$ is the prefix cumulative loss.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Prefix potential]
\lean{prefixPotential}
\label{prefixPotential}
\leanok
\uses{ZeroSumGame, prefixHedgeWeight}
The \emph{prefix potential} is the sum of prefix Hedge weights over all rows:
\[
  \Phi_t \;=\; \sum_{i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,M} w_t(i).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Positivity of the prefix Hedge weight]
\lean{prefixHedgeWeight_pos}
\label{prefixHedgeWeight_pos}
\leanok
\uses{ZeroSumGame, prefixHedgeWeight}
\difficulty{1}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M$ row actions and $N$ column
actions, let $\eta \in \bbr$ be a learning rate, and fix any prefix $a_0, \dots,
a_{t-1}$ of $t$ column actions together with a row $i$. Then the prefix Hedge weight
$w_t(i) = \exp\!\bigl(-\eta \cdot L_t(i)\bigr)$ is strictly positive, where $L_t(i) =
\sum_{s=0}^{t-1}\bigl(1 - A_{i,a_s}\bigr)$ is the prefix cumulative loss of row $i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Positivity of the prefix potential]
\lean{prefixPotential_pos}
\label{prefixPotential_pos}
\leanok
\uses{ZeroSumGame, prefixHedgeWeight_pos, prefixPotential}
\difficulty{2}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with at least one row action, fix a
learning rate $\eta \in \bbr$, and let $a_0, \dots, a_{t-1}$ be any prefix of column
actions. Then the prefix potential is strictly positive,
\[
  \Phi_t \;=\; \sum_{i} \exp\!\bigl(-\eta\, L_t(i)\bigr) \;>\; 0,
\]
where $L_t(i)$ is the prefix cumulative loss of row $i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Prefix Hedge mixed strategy]
\lean{prefixHedgeMixedStrategy}
\label{prefixHedgeMixedStrategy}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, ZeroSumGame, prefixHedgeWeight, prefixHedgeWeight_pos, prefixPotential, prefixPotential_pos}
The normalised Hedge distribution after a prefix of $t$ column actions is the
mixed row strategy with weights
\[
  p_t(i) \;=\; \frac{w_t(i)}{\Phi_t},
\]
where $w_t(i)$ is the prefix Hedge weight and $\Phi_t$ the prefix potential.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Online column best responses to Hedge]
\lean{hedgeResponseNat}
\label{hedgeResponseNat}
\leanok
\uses{ZeroSumGame, bestColumn, prefixHedgeMixedStrategy}
The sequence of column best responses generated online against Hedge: at time
$t$, given the history $a_0, \dots, a_{t-1}$ of prior column choices, the
column player responds with $a_t = \mathrm{bestColumn}(G, p_t)$, where $p_t$
is the prefix Hedge mixed strategy.  This is defined by well-founded recursion
on $t$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Prefix game loss equals induced cumulative loss]
\lean{prefixGameLoss_eq_cumLoss}
\label{prefixGameLoss_eq_cumLoss}
\leanok
\uses{ZeroSumGame, ZeroSumGame.toLossSeq, cumLoss, prefixGameLoss}
\difficulty{4}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M$ row actions and $N$ column
actions, given by a payoff matrix $A$ with $0 \le A_{ij} \le 1$, and let $a_0, \dots,
a_{T-1}$ be a sequence of column actions with each $a_s \in \mathrm{Fin}\,N$. Fix a row
action $i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,M$ and a round $t \in \mathrm{Fin}\,T$. Then the prefix
cumulative loss of row $i$ along the first $t$ column actions coincides with the
cumulative loss of expert $i$ through the first $t$ rounds of the loss sequence induced
by $G$ and $(a_s)_s$; that is,
\[
\sum_{s=0}^{t-1} \bigl(1 - A_{i,\,a_s}\bigr) \;=\; \sum_{s < t} \bigl(1 -
A_{i,\,a_s}\bigr).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Prefix Hedge weight agrees with the induced-loss Hedge weight]
\lean{prefixHedgeWeight_eq_hedgeWeight}
\label{prefixHedgeWeight_eq_hedgeWeight}
\leanok
\uses{ZeroSumGame, ZeroSumGame.toLossSeq, hedgeWeight, prefixGameLoss_eq_cumLoss, prefixHedgeWeight}
\difficulty{2}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M$ row actions and $N$ column
actions, with payoff matrix $A$, let $\eta \in \bbr$ be a learning rate, and let $a_0,
\dots, a_{T-1}$ be a sequence of column actions, so that $a : \mathrm{Fin}\,T \to
\mathrm{Fin}\,N$. Fix a round $t \in \mathrm{Fin}\,T$ and a row $i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,M$.
Then the prefix Hedge weight of row $i$ at learning rate $\eta$, computed from the
length-$t$ prefix $a_0, \dots, a_{t-1}$ of column actions, equals the Hedge weight of
expert $i$ at time $t$ and learning rate $\eta$ for the loss sequence $\ell_s(j) = 1 -
A_{j, a_s}$ induced by $G$ along $a$; that is, both equal
\[
  \exp\!\Bigl(-\eta \sum_{s < t} \bigl(1 - A_{i, a_s}\bigr)\Bigr).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Prefix potential equals the induced Hedge potential]
\lean{prefixPotential_eq_potential}
\label{prefixPotential_eq_potential}
\leanok
\uses{ZeroSumGame, ZeroSumGame.toLossSeq, potential, prefixHedgeWeight_eq_hedgeWeight, prefixPotential}
\difficulty{2}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with payoff matrix $A$ having $M$ rows and
$N$ columns, fix a learning rate $\eta \in \bbr$, and let $a_0, \dots, a_{T-1}$ be a
sequence of $T$ column actions. For any round $t < T$, the prefix potential of $G$ at
learning rate $\eta$ formed from the first $t$ column actions $a_0, \dots, a_{t-1}$
equals the Hedge potential at time $t$ of the loss sequence $\ell_s(i) = 1 - A_{i, a_s}$
induced on the row player by $G$ and the full sequence of column actions; that is, \[
\sum_{i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,M} \exp\!\Bigl(-\eta \sum_{s=0}^{t-1}\bigl(1 - A_{i,
a_s}\bigr)\Bigr) \;=\; \sum_{i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,M} \exp\!\bigl(-\eta\, L_t(i)\bigr), \]
where $L_t(i) = \sum_{s < t} \ell_s(i)$ is the cumulative loss of row $i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Prefix Hedge strategy agrees with the abstract Hedge distribution]
\lean{prefixHedgeMixedStrategy_weight_eq_hedgeDist}
\label{prefixHedgeMixedStrategy_weight_eq_hedgeDist}
\leanok
\uses{ZeroSumGame, ZeroSumGame.toLossSeq, hedgeDist, prefixHedgeMixedStrategy, prefixHedgeWeight_eq_hedgeWeight, prefixPotential_eq_potential}
\difficulty{2}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M \ge 1$ row actions and $N$ column
actions, fix a learning rate $\eta \in \bbr$, and let $a_0, \dots, a_{T-1}$ be a
sequence of column actions. For any round $t < T$ and any row $i$, the weight assigned
to $i$ by the prefix Hedge mixed strategy built from the length-$t$ prefix $a_0, \dots,
a_{t-1}$ equals the Hedge distribution value $p_t(i)$ obtained by running abstract
Hedge, at the same learning rate $\eta$, on the loss sequence $\ell$ induced by $G$ and
$a$, namely $\ell_s(i) = 1 - A_{i, a_s}$. In symbols, both sides equal $w_t(i)/\Phi_t$,
where $w_t(i) = \exp(-\eta \sum_{s<t}(1 - A_{i,a_s}))$ and $\Phi_t = \sum_{k} w_t(k)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Regret-to-payoff bridge for zero-sum games]
\lean{regret_to_payoff}
\label{regret_to_payoff}
\leanok
\uses{ZeroSumGame}
\difficulty{5}
Consider a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M \ge 1$ row actions and $N$ column
actions and payoff matrix $A$, every entry of which satisfies $0 \le A_{ij} \le 1$,
played over $T \ge 1$ rounds. Suppose that in each round $t$ the row player commits to a
probability distribution $p_t$ over the row actions (so $\sum_i p_t(i) = 1$) while the
column player chooses an action $j_t$, and that the cumulative loss regret is bounded by
$R$:
\[
  \sum_t \sum_i p_t(i)\,\bigl(1 - A_{i,j_t}\bigr)
  \;-\; \min_i \sum_t \bigl(1 - A_{i,j_t}\bigr) \;\le\; R,
\]
where the minimum runs over the row actions. Then the row player's cumulative expected
payoff satisfies
\[
  \sum_t \sum_i p_t(i)\,A_{i,j_t}
  \;\ge\;
  \max_i \sum_t A_{i,j_t} \;-\; R,
\]
with the maximum taken over the row actions.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Average of pointwise minima at most minimum of averages]
\lean{avg_min_le_min_avg}
\label{avg_min_le_min_avg}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $N \ge 1$ and $T \ge 1$ be integers, and let $f(t,j)$ be a real number for each $t
\in \{1,\dots,T\}$ and each $j \in \{1,\dots,N\}$. Then averaging over $t$ before
minimising over $j$ can only increase the value:
\[
  \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^{T} \min_{1 \le j \le N} f(t,j)
  \;\le\;
  \min_{1 \le j \le N} \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t=1}^{T} f(t,j).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Hedge yields an approximate minimax pair]
\lean{hedge_construction}
\label{hedge_construction}
\leanok
\uses{LossSeq, LossSeq.Valid, MixedStrategy, ZeroSumGame, ZeroSumGame.toLossSeq, ZeroSumGame.toLossSeq_valid, averageStrategy, bestColumn, bestColumn_spec, bestExpertLoss, cumLoss_horizon, empiricalStrategy, hedgeCumLoss, hedgeDist, hedgeDist_nonneg, hedgeDist_sum, hedgeLoss, hedgeResponseNat, hedge_regret_bound_tight, payoffVsPure, payoffVsPure_averageStrategy, prefixHedgeMixedStrategy, prefixHedgeMixedStrategy_weight_eq_hedgeDist, pureVsPayoff, pureVsPayoff_empiricalStrategy, regret, regret_to_payoff}
\difficulty{6}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with $M \ge 2$ row actions and $N \ge 1$
column actions, with payoff matrix $(A_{ij})$ satisfying $0 \le A_{ij} \le 1$; the row
player maximises and the column player minimises. Fix an integer $T > 0$ and a learning
rate $\eta > 0$. Then there exist a mixed row strategy $p$ and a mixed column strategy
$q$ such that, for every pure row $i \in \{1,\dots,M\}$ and every pure column $j \in
\{1,\dots,N\}$,
\[
  \sum_{i'} p_{i'}\,A_{i'j} \;+\; \frac{(\ln M)/\eta + \eta T/8}{T}
  \;\ge\;
  \sum_{j'} A_{ij'}\,q_{j'}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Approximate minimax for finite zero-sum games]
\lean{approx_minimax}
\statementsource{raoyehudayoff-ch03-randomized-protocols}{pdf-3eebfb23ab53-p004-b003}
\label{approx_minimax}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, ZeroSumGame, hedge_construction, payoffVsPure, pureVsPayoff}
\difficulty{5}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with payoff matrix $A$, having $M \ge 2$
row actions and at least one column action, and let $\varepsilon > 0$. Then there exist
a mixed row strategy $p$ and a mixed column strategy $q$ that form an
$\varepsilon$-approximate saddle point: for every pure row $i$ and every pure column
$j$,
\[
  \sum_{k} p_k\, A_{kj} \;+\; \varepsilon \;\ge\; \sum_{\ell} A_{i\ell}\, q_\ell .
\]
That is, up to an additive $\varepsilon$, the expected payoff of $p$ against any pure
column is at least the expected payoff of any pure row against $q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Approximate minimax theorem for finite zero-sum games]
\lean{minimax_approx_theorem}
\statementsource{raoyehudayoff-ch03-randomized-protocols}{pdf-3eebfb23ab53-p004-b003}
\label{minimax_approx_theorem}
\leanok
\uses{MixedStrategy, ZeroSumGame, approx_minimax, payoffVsPure, pureVsPayoff}
\difficulty{1}
Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game with payoff matrix $A$, having at least two
row actions and at least one column action, and suppose every entry satisfies $0 \le
A_{ij} \le 1$. Then for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exist a mixed row strategy $p$ and
a mixed column strategy $q$ such that, for every pure row $i$ and every pure column $j$,
\[
  \sum_{k} p_k \, A_{kj} + \varepsilon \;\ge\; \sum_{\ell} A_{i\ell} \, q_\ell.
\]
That is, the row player's guaranteed payoff under $p$ against any column falls short of
the column player's exposure under $q$ against any row by at most $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}
